A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the COLIPRI research work. Their main texts, figures, tables, equations, and complete appendices are readable, allowing reliable matching across substantial reorganization and scientific revisions.

before.justification: v1 reports original pre-training ablations, classification experiments on CT-RATE and RAD-ChestCT, report-generation results, and segmentation experiments.

after.justification: v2 reports original experiments for the revised COLIPRI encoders, including classification, report generation, retrieval, segmentation, and component ablations in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: v2 introduces the Opposite Sentence Loss, constructing positive/negated sentence pairs and combining their supervision equally with CLIP alignment (Sections 3.2.1 and B.4). It also initializes the MAE-containing encoders with MAE-pretrained weights and includes MAE throughout training, replacing v1's late inclusion. These change the training procedure substantially.

E1.justification: v2 adds the HVS segmentation dataset, covering hepatic vessels and adjacent tumours in 303 cases (Section 4.2). CT-RATE, NLST, RAD-ChestCT, LiTS, Lung, and KiTS23 remain. The broader dataset catalogue in Table A.1 does not establish additional training or evaluation coverage.

E2.justification: v2 adds MedImageInsight and Curia to classification and report-generation comparisons, adds the pure MAE encoder to classification probing, and adds default nnU-Net and ResEnc-L segmentation references. CT-CLIP also becomes a reported retrieval comparator. BIUD and fVLM already participated in v1's zero-shot comparisons.

E3.justification: Segmentation expands from the first three cross-validation folds to all five. v2 reports 250k-step comparisons alongside 37.5k-step results, although v1 Appendix C.6 already mentioned the longer schedule. Retrieval evaluation specifies deduplication and adds mean/median rank. Zero-shot results distinguish all-class and fVLM-matched evaluations, while thresholded classification metrics are removed.

E4.justification: v2 adds direct ablations testing whether OSL closes the short/native prompt gap (Table 3) and whether MAE initialization enables effective segmentation transfer (Table D.5). Figure D.1 adds abnormality-specific report-generation analysis. Most earlier hyperparameter sweeps are retained in Appendix B; their relocation is not new analytical evidence.

E5.justification: Uncertainty reporting expands to probing and zero-shot classification through 95% confidence intervals based on 100 bootstrap samples (Tables 1–2). Report-generation intervals already existed in v1; v2 newly specifies their 95% level, median estimates, and 500 bootstrap samples. These reporting additions do not establish additional independent training runs.

E6.justification: Results for the revised encoders change substantially. COLIPRI-CRM's CT-RATE probe AUPRC changes from 56.65 to 61.28 (v1 Table 7; v2 Table 1). Its report-generation RadBERT macro F1 changes from 39.7 to 44.9, while RadFact-CT logical F1 (+/-) falls from 69.2 to 66.9 (Table 9 versus D.2). New retrieval, HVS, and long-schedule results appear; segmentation averages also use different fold counts.

T1.justification: Appendix B.4 adds formal definitions for OSL sentence sampling, supervision labels, pair probabilities, and the combined alignment objective (Equations 1–7). This is a mathematical formulation of a new training component. Neither version develops theoretical guarantees or proofs.

C1.justification: v2 makes OSL an explicit novel contribution and strengthens the claimed outcome from strong global-task performance with limited dense-task benefits to state-of-the-art performance across tasks. In particular, the abstract replaces v1's competitive segmentation claim with a state-of-the-art claim, echoed in the conclusion.

C2.justification: v1 interprets weak segmentation gains as limited compatibility between global alignment and voxel reconstruction. v2 emphasizes MAE initialization and continued MAE training, and discusses remaining limitations relative to CNNs and degradation under longer fine-tuning. It also expands clinical qualifications concerning insufficient accuracy, dataset diversity, and the need for evaluation stratified by findings and patient characteristics.

D1.justification: v2 announces access to COLIPRI weights, inference code, and examples; adds final configuration Tables B.8–B.10, OSL sampling/padding pseudocode, exact split counts, and NIfTI-Zarr preprocessing/storage details. These substantially improve documentation. Some settings remain inconsistent: Table B.8 specifies a COLIPRI-C learning rate of 6e-5, while Section B.1.4 retains 6e-4.

R1.justification: The central positioning around combining 3D vision-language learning, report generation, and self-supervision remains. v2 updates the supporting literature, adding 2D medical VLE references and new baseline citations while removing some broad natural-image background. Appendix B.4.2 additionally positions OSL against Merlin and fVLM's organ-based approaches.

P1.justification: The narrative is substantially reorganized: v1's development framework and extensive method-development experiments move into Appendices A–B, while v2 presents a compact standalone Method section followed by experiments and results. The introduction, related work, discussion, and conclusion are extensively rewritten. The original report-processing prompts are largely retained.

P2.justification: Figure 2 is redrawn into four objective-specific panels. The PCA comparison moves to the first page and retains only COLIPRI-CRM among the proposed variants. Classification and segmentation tables are restructured, detailed report-generation results move to Appendix D, and new configuration tables, an algorithm display, and an abnormality-wise plot are added.

improvement.justification: v2 addresses two important weaknesses identified in v1—short-prompt brittleness and weak dense-task transfer—with explicit method changes and targeted ablations (Tables 3 and D.5). Expanded baseline comparisons, uncertainty reporting, and implementation documentation substantially strengthen the paper's evidence and reproducibility. The blanket segmentation superiority claim exceeds the CNN comparisons in Table 5, and configuration inconsistencies remain, but these caveats do not outweigh the substantial gains.
